name: curl
summary: Transfer data from or to a URL, within the web access the application allows
help: Usage: curl [options...] <url>...
Fetch each URL and write the response body to standard output.
-d, --data <data>          send <data> in a POST body (@FILE reads a file, @- stdin; newlines dropped)
--data-binary <data>   like --data, but the file is sent exactly as it is
--data-raw <data>      like --data, but @ has no special meaning
--data-urlencode <d>   like --data, URL-encoding the value (name=value, =value, value)
--json <data>          send <data> as JSON (sets Content-Type and Accept)
-G, --get                  send the --data values as a query string in a GET
-X, --request <method>     use <method> instead of GET or POST
-H, --header <header>      add a request header ("Name: value")
-A, --user-agent <name>    set the User-Agent header
-u, --user <user:pass>     use HTTP basic authentication
-L, --location             follow redirects
--max-redirs <num>     follow at most <num> redirects
-i, --include              print the response headers before the body
-I, --head                 send a HEAD request and print the headers
-o, --output <file>        write the body to <file> instead of standard output
-O, --remote-name          write the body to a file named like the URL's last part
-f, --fail                 exit 22 without printing the body when the status is 400 or more
--fail-with-body       like --fail, but print the body
-s, --silent               print no error messages
-S, --show-error           print error messages even with --silent
-w, --write-out <format>   print <format> after the transfer, e.g. '%{http_code}'
-m, --max-time <seconds>   give up after <seconds>
--compressed           ask for a compressed response and decompress it
-v, --verbose              print the request and response headers on standard error
-k, --insecure             accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified
-h, --help                 show this help
-V, --version              show the version
The application decides which sites can be reached; others fail like an unknown host.
tryHelp: curl: try 'curl --help' or 'curl --manual' for more information

send DATA URL-encoded (name=value encodes only the value)
send DATA as a JSON POST body with JSON Content-Type and Accept headers
put the data in the query string of a GET instead of a POST body
the request method
an extra request header, "Name: value" ("Name:" removes a default one)
the User-Agent header
basic authentication
follow redirects, each one checked against the web policy
the most redirects to follow (never more than the policy allows)
print the status line and response headers before the body
send HEAD and print the status line and headers
write the body to FILE
write the body to the file the URL's last path segment names
fail with exit status 22 and no body on a status of 400 or more
fail with exit status 22 on a status of 400 or more, after printing the body
no error messages
error messages even when silent

exitCodes.1: unsupported or disallowed protocol, or a request the web policy refuses
exitCodes.6: host not resolved, or not allowed by the web policy
exitCodes.7: could not connect (an IP address the web policy refuses)
exitCodes.22: --fail and a status of 400 or more
exitCodes.23: could not write the output file
exitCodes.26: could not read a data file
exitCodes.63: response larger than the web policy allows

messages.readFile: curl: option {option}: error encountered when reading a file
messages.badNumber: curl: option {option}: expected a proper numerical parameter
messages.protocol: Protocol "{scheme}" not supported or disabled in libcurl
messages.badUrl: URL rejected: Malformed input to a URL function
messages.connect: Failed to connect to {host} port {port} after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server
messages.timeout: Operation timed out after {ms} milliseconds with {bytes} bytes received
messages.noRemoteName: Failed writing received data to disk/application
messages.badHeader: A libcurl function was given a bad argument
messages.recv: Failure when receiving data from the peer
messages.tls: SSL certificate problem: unable to verify the certificate of {host}
messages.replay: Topwater replay: {request} is not in the recording
messages.reasonPrivate: {host} is a private or reserved address
messages.reasonResolvesPrivate: {host} resolves to a private or reserved address
messages.reasonBody: the request body is larger than {limit} bytes
messages.reasonCallLimit: the limit of {limit} requests in one call was reached
messages.reasonSessionLimit: the limit of {limit} requests for this session was reached
messages.reasonNoCredential: the credentials for {host} are not available
messages.reasonBadCredential: the credentials for {host} are not a valid header value

notes: The reason* messages are the web policy's reasons, shared with wget (WebSession builds them). Registered in every shell; without a web policy (Shell.AllowWeb and the ports' equivalents) every host fails to resolve, as on a machine without a network. No progress meter is printed.
